audit.whatIsWrong: 'While his R is active he's immune to your E slow and your R suppress' — and elsewhere 'the one lockdown his Ragnarok can't pre-empt'. The entry states the interaction two contradictory ways and gets the scope wrong in both.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Olaf passively gains increased armor and magic resist. He can activate this ability to become immune to disables for as long as he keeps attacking.' Three things follow. The immunity is to disables, so it answers your suppression and your slam stun directly — it is not something the R sneaks past. It is conditional: it lasts only as long as he keeps attacking, so a target that walks out of his range ends it. And the passive half means he is carrying free armour and MR against your all-physical damage from level 6 whether he presses it or not.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text, spikes[3].text, mid, wants.foe[0] and whys[4] now state the disable immunity, the keep-attacking condition and the passive resistances.

audit.whatIsWrong: Berserker Rage is never named, so the entry's advice to chunk him and disengage is given without the thing that makes it dangerous.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Olaf gains Attack Speed and Life Steal based on his missing Health.' A half-health Olaf attacks faster and heals more than a full-health one. Trading him to 50% and standing there is how the trade flips. It also explains Reckless Swing: he pays his own health to cast it, which feeds the passive rather than weakening him.
audit.corrected: Added to early, whys[0] and late.
sources: champ-data/_kits/olaf.json (P Berserker Rage, E Reckless Swing)

audit.whatIsWrong: Undertow is described only as an axe slow, and Tough It Out is not mentioned anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: Undertow is a flat 9 seconds from 1000 range and it reduces armour as well as move speed — against a physical-damage Ambessa that shred is his damage amp, not just a kiting tool — and picking the axe back up resets the cooldown outright, so the 9 seconds is a ceiling, not a expectation. Tough It Out is 16/15/14/13/12 and gives him attack speed and a shield, which is the cooldown that decides whether your burst window is real.
audit.corrected: Named in spikes[0].text, early, wants.foe[1], whys[1], breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d.
sources: champ-data/_kits/olaf.json (Q Undertow, W Tough It Out)

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Your W shield does nothing against the true damage' and 'E's true-damage nuke your W shield can't block'.
audit.why: Nothing in Riot's text for Repudiation or for Reckless Swing supports a shield being bypassed. The kit data does not answer whether shields absorb true damage, so this is a mechanic the entry asserts without a source. What is in the text and worth saying instead: Reckless Swing deals true damage, so armour does nothing about it, and it costs Olaf health he refunds only if it destroys the target.
audit.corrected: Both replaced with the verifiable version — true damage ignores armour, and the self-cost feeds Berserker Rage.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'While his Ragnarok is on cooldown' and 'strictly around his R timer' are the entry's core instruction, and the timer is never given.
audit.why: Ragnarok is 100/90/80 against Public Execution's 130/115/100. His ultimate comes back thirty seconds sooner than hers at rank 1 — so 'fight on his R cooldown' is a narrower window than it sounds, and spending hers into an active Ragnarok wastes the longer of the two. The supporting numbers: Undertow flat 9s, Reckless Swing 11s at rank 1, Tough It Out 16s.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to spikes[2].text, mid, late, whys[5], breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text and mid say Public Execution 'blinks behind him'.
audit.why: Riot's text: it 'blinks to the farthest enemy champion in a line of her choosing'. Champion, not position — and after lane that means a deeper-standing enemy takes the blink instead of Olaf.
audit.corrected: Both now say the farthest champion in the line.

edits.before: Olaf owns this opening and you can't trade it straight — you've got one ability, you're energy-gated, and his E (Reckless Swing) hits you with a true-damage nuke your W shield can't soak. His Q (Undertow) axe slows you so you can't kite or disengage, and if he walks over the thrown axe to retrieve it the Q cooldown refunds and he's perma-aggressive with lifesteal topping him back up. Don't try to dash-weave in at 1-3; last-hit at the edge of your Q's cone, eat minimal poke, and don't burn E chasing — he'll just out-trade and heal it off.
edits.after: Olaf owns this opening and you can't trade it straight — you've got one ability, you're energy-gated, and Reckless Swing is true damage no armour reduces. It costs him health to cast, but Berserker Rage gives him attack speed and lifesteal off missing health, so hurting him partly pays him back. Undertow slows you and strips your armour from 1000, and picking the axe up resets its 9s outright, so he can be perma-aggressive. Don't dash-weave in at 1-3; last-hit at the blades of your cone and don't burn E chasing.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are still his — your cooldowns are longest and his Q-slow into E true damage out-trades your empowered autos before you can chain a full combo. The lane flips at 6: your R blinks behind him, suppresses and stuns, and that lockdown is the one thing his kit genuinely fears. But the whole fight hinges on his Ragnarok — if he presses R first, your E slow and R suppress do nothing and his autos cut through your W shield. So bait it: fake commitment, make him burn R, then unload your full combo on the cooldown.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are still his — your cooldowns are longest and Undertow into Reckless Swing out-trades your empowered autos before you chain a full combo. The lane flips at 6: your R blinks to the farthest champion in the line, suppresses and stuns, and that lockdown is the one thing his kit genuinely fears. But it hinges on Ragnarok — while it is up he is immune to disables for as long as he keeps attacking, so the suppress never lands. Bait it: fake the commit, make him burn a 100s ultimate, then unload.

Pick your all-ins strictly around his R timer, look to roam and snowball elsewhere with R's pick potential, and don't try to farm-lane him out — straight up he edges the duel.

notes: The Ragnarok interaction was stated two contradictory ways in the same entry — 'the one lockdown his Ragnarok can't pre-empt' in one spike and 'immune to your R suppress' in another. Riot's text settles it: he is immune to disables while it is active, so Public Execution's suppression is precisely what it answers, and hers is 130s against his 100s. The keep-attacking condition and the passive armour/MR half were both missing and both matter. I also removed 'your W shield does nothing against the true damage': whether a shield absorbs true damage is not answerable from the kit data, so I replaced it with what is in the text — Reckless Swing is true damage, armour does nothing, and its self-cost feeds Berserker Rage. Two abilities were entirely absent from the matchup: Tough It Out (16s shield plus attack speed) and the armour shred half of Undertow, which is his damage amp against an all-physical opponent.
